<a id="blowhorn-classify-url"></a>

Say what a link is, by the platform rules the engine keeps: `post` when it names an existing post or comment on a supported platform, with the verbs that platform takes (`respond`, `amplify`); `page` for any other web link, with the platform whose site it is on; `none` for anything that is not a web link. The desktop app's drop reads this to choose its sheet. It reads the link text only: it opens no browser, signs in to nothing and writes nothing.

```text
blowhorn classify-url [OPTIONS] url
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | yes | The link to classify |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit the classification as JSON with a stable shape, for a script or the desktop app |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn classify-url`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn classify-url` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
| `--risk-profile` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn classify-url` because `--risk-profile` is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn classify-url 'https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7123456789012345678/' --json
blowhorn classify-url https://example.com/article
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.
